To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the experimentally measured baryon stopping is an indication of a non-monotonously increasing stopping with the incident energy of heavy ion collisions and that the mixed phase is a possible explanation for this behavior.

the observed irregularity in baryon stopping is a clear signal for the onset of the mixed-phase formation, which in the case of the first-order phase transition is expected at the incident energy of about 8 GeV/nucleon.
the experimentally measured irregularities in baryon stopping are reproduced only by models involving the phase transition into quark-gluonic phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for the mixed phase of strongly interacting matter in heavy-ion collisions at intermediate energies (1–10 AGeV).
the search for a signal of the onset of the first-order phase transition in heavy-ion collisions.
the study of baryon stopping in heavy-ion collisions and its dependence on the incident energy of the colliding nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed baryon-stopping irregularities in the incident energy dependence can be a signal of the onset of the mixed phase of the nuclear matter.
the experimentally measured baryon stopping in heavy-ion collisions is not yet fully understood.
the baryon stopping as well as the irregularity in the net-proton excitation function can be a signature of the mixed-phase formation in heavy-ion collisions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the observed baryon-stopping signal is a strong hint of the existence of a first-order phase-transition in nuclear matter.
the baryon stopping in heavy-ion collisions is not a unique signal of a phase transition, but it is rather a signal of the onset of the mixed-phase.

a first-order phase-transition scenario with a crossover one into a quark-gluonic phase is the most promising scenario, but that more detailed investigations with a more realistic hadronic EoS, a more sophisticated treatment of the phase transition, and a more realistic treatment of baryon stopping are required to make a definite statement on whether the observed irregularity of the baryon stopping is a signal of the phase transition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mixed phase of nuclear matter is a necessary condition for the observed irregularity of baryon stopping, but not a sufficient one.
baryon stopping is a sensitive signal of the onset of the mixed phase.
the experimentally measured baryon stopping is not a signal of the onset of a first-order phase-transition in the EoS of nuclear matter.
